One of the best things about watching a good crime show is putting on your detective hat and trying to figure out who the killer is. Normally, these criminals are trying to conceal themselves, hiding in the shadows so they won’t be so easily caught. Normally, these criminals will try to blend into society, taking on roles such as being a sheriff or a highly respected member of the community, to throw people off the scent of who they really are. We call this hiding in plain sight, and it's been a bedrock of crime shows for decades. These killers walk among the population, blending in with the crowd, which makes the detective’s job that much harder to do, and has the audience believe that they couldn't possibly be responsible for such heinous crimes. So, when the killer is revealed, and it’s a person no one would ever expect, it brings a sense of shock and awe to the audience, who were so convinced that the blood expert at the police department, or the former U.S. Marine, was not the killer. Oh, but they were, and these reveals are the ultimate “got you” moments. With that in mind, let’s take a good look at the best crime shows where the killer was hiding among us the entire time. These shows are absolutely famous for having their killers hide in plain sight, and contain reveals that are still talked about to this very day. 7 'Mindhunter' (2017–2019) Holt McCallany and Jonathan Groff show a crime scene photo to someone off-screen in Mindhunter. Image via Netflix When it comes to shows that hide their killers in plain sight, no show did it better than Netflix’s Mindhunter . Based on the true crime book Mindhunter: Inside the FBI’s Elite Serial Crime Unit , the series follows the book’s path in breaking down the psychology of some of the world’s most notorious serial killers in order to solve cases. By implementing this logic, viewers were able to get a terrifying look inside the mind of a serial killer and use this to find out who the killer was. Oftentimes, the killer we were searching for was right there in front of us, and we didn't even know it. All we had to do was think like them to crack the case. That was Mindhunter ’s biggest strength: getting viewers to think like a serial killer to solve the case and find out who the killer actually was. There were times when the killer was just as we suspected it would be, and other times, it caught us completely by surprise. If you’re tuning into Mindhunter for the first time, be prepared to be stunned by some jaw-dropping reveals as to who the criminal actually is. 6 'The Following' (2013–2015) Kevin Bacon as Ryan Hardy, looking surprised on 'The Following' Image via Fox In the mid-2010s, Fox was on the lookout for a hit crime drama, and they thought The Following , starring Kevin Bacon and James Purefoy , would be that hit. In the end, it didn’t prove to be a success, being canceled after just three seasons, and soon becoming forgotten. That’s a shame, as this series was quite innovative for its time, especially when it came to its central antagonist, serial killer Joe Carroll (Purefoy), who was one mean dude. Carroll was not a killer to be messed with, especially after he broke out of prison, and Bacon’s character, FBI agent Ryan Hardy, and other agents, hot on his tail to apprehend him and take him back to the slammer. As the show moved along, though, finding him and getting him back to prison would not be so easy. Why? Well, they soon learn that Carroll had amassed an army of fanatical killers that follows him, with Emma Hill ( Valorie Curry ) as his second-in-command of sorts. Even worse, we, the audience, didn’t really know who was a normal person, and who was one of Carroll’s sick killers . That was the beauty of The Following , an engaging crime drama , but it also had a good bit of psychological horror mixed in and managed to fool us in each episode. 5 'The Mentalist' (2008–2015) Simon Baker as Patrick Jane and Robin Tunney as Lisbon looking concerned in The Mentalist. Image via CBS You would think that a show featuring a psychic who uses his “abilities” to read people’s minds and solve murder cases would know who the killer was before we, the audience, did. But here in The Mentalist , CBS’ hit slow-burn crime drama that ran for seven seasons, there were some killers that were clearly hiding among us, even some that we didn’t know were there until the final reveal. Most of the cases on The Mentalist revolved around Red John, a serial killer who was responsible for the murder of Patrick Jane’s ( Simon Baker ) family. While we were all tuned in to see Jane use his “powers” (spoiler alert: he had no psychic powers) to try to find the man who murdered his wife and child, we didn’t know who he was until Season 6, when it was revealed that Red John was the sheriff of Napa County, Thomas McAllister ( Xander Berkeley ). Talk about having the perfect cover . No one could believe that Red John, a serial killer, became a sheriff, hiding his crime from all of us. Touché, Mr. McAllister, touché. 4 'Barry' (2018–2023) Barry Berkman and Gene Cousineau standing onstage together in Barry. Image via HBO One can look at HBO’s Barry as a spiritual successor, of sorts, to Dexter . They both kind of had the same premise, except Barry took on a more comedic tone than Dexter did, so much so that you would be more focused on the hilarity that ensued than on the killer that was hiding in plain sight. Nevertheless, Barry was just as good as Showtime’s famed series, especially with the writers deciding to hide the true identity of Barry Berkman ( Bill Hader ), a former U.S. Marine-turned-hitman. When he gets an assignment that takes him to L.A. to make sure a target stops living, he joins an acting class that allows him to question whether or not life as an assassin is worth it. The hilarious part of Barry is that we watched the entire time a group of acting students sit among a hitman , talking and befriending Barry, while not knowing his true identity. The entire idea of hiding in plain sight is to act and do things that won’t let you stand out and be exposed to the person that you truly are, and Barry did this to perfection. 3 'Killing Eve' (2018–2022) Jodie Comer as Villanelle holds a knife to Sandra Oh as Eve in the kitchen in Killing Eve. Image via BBC America For four seasons, we were enthralled by the drama that was pulsating from Killing Eve , a woman-led spy show that had a multitude of killers who we didn’t know were among the population of the series. With Villanelle ( Jodie Comer ), the main antagonist of the series, it wasn’t until Season 2 that we began to see a new villain that Villanelle and MI6 agent Eve Polastri ( Sandra Oh ) had to work together to defeat, one that was practically invisible. She was so invisible that she was nicknamed “The Ghost,” an assassin who was an expert at hiding in plain sight . Not only that, but the introduction of “The Ghost” in Season 2 served as a way for the showrunners to divide the women of the series, one who openly stands out, and others who want to blend in. It was one of Killing Eve ’s more unique aspects , and made you pay attention to every episode so that you wouldn't miss the clues that were laid out right there for us to see. 2 'Twin Peaks' (1990–1991) Kyle Maclachlan as Special Agent Dale Cooper in twin Peaks Image via ABC Although the original series of ABC’s Twin Peaks ran for just two seasons, it is still one of the most talked-about shows of all time, especially when it comes to its central premise: who killed Laura Palmer ( Sheryl Lee) ? When we found out who killed her, it was safe to say that we were all shocked, as the mystery played out beautifully. The killer turned out to be Laura’s own father, Leland Palmer ( Ray Wise ), who was one of the most respected residents of the town. No one, and we mean no one, would have ever suspected this turn of events, especially the way the writers told the story. To this day, the reveal of Laura Palmer’s killer is one of the best twists in TV history , one that was clearly hiding in plain sight among us. 1 'Dexter' (2006–2013) Michael C. Hall as Dexter Morgan piping a blood sample in the pilot episode of 'Dexter'. Image via Showtime When it comes to killers hiding in plain sight, few do it better than Dexter Morgan ( Michael C. Hall ) of the iconic Showtime series Dexter . The series, which ran for eight seasons, was a masterclass in hiding its central killer from the audience. The title character was a bloodstain pattern analyst for the Miami Police Department. Being part of law enforcement, you wouldn’t think that there was anything suspicious about Dexter, but you would be so, so wrong. By day, Dexter was a bloodstain expert for the cops, but by night, he was a vigilante serial killer , dispensing justice to murderers who didn’t get the punishment they were due through the justice system. So, in a sense, Dexter was the classic anti-hero, but, nevertheless, he was a killer that hid in plain sight, and a good one at that. Colour Melting Inspiration How to Maintain Your Colour Melt By Mica Ricketts published 27 November 2025 in Features Now that the nights are drawing in and the cold weather is upon us, those who love switching up their hair colour with the seasons might be wondering what the trending tones will be for winter. This year, however, it’s less about one viral shade (like deep burgundy ) and more about one specific technique that colourists are raving about. Enter: colour melting. Unlike balayage or highlights, which use ribbons of colour and defined points of contrast to add brightness and depth, colour melting takes a more diffused approach to hair colour for a more effortless and luxurious result. Trust us—it’s what everyone is going to be asking for in salons as we head into 2026. A post shared by Mary Phillips (@maryphillips) A photo posted by on What is Colour Melting? “Colour melting creates a seamless blend from one tone to the next, with no visible lines or obvious colour marks. It’s so smooth that it could actually be mistaken for your natural hair,” explains Nicole Kahlani , concept colourist at Hershesons Fitzrovia. The difference between more popular colour techniques like balayage or highlights is that colour melting is less about creating contrast and instead tends to use a “global application”, which is where colour is applied all over the head rather than just in certain sections, to make sure that “every shade flows effortlessly into the next”. The result is exactly as the name suggests—a melting between colours for a soft, understated and effortlessly natural look. This also means that colour melting is an incredibly versatile technique that works well with all hair tones—coppers, blondes, reds and brunettes. “All shades work with hair melting, but you do need to use at least three colours to create that blend,” explains Siobhan Haug , colour specialist and Co-Founder of Haug London Haus. “In fact, the funny thing is that the more colour you put in, the more natural the gradient appears. Sign in to your Collider account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Dramatic television has evolved significantly over the past decade, largely due to the streaming wars, which have enabled various networks and studios to pursue niche content. While there are certainly intentions to create more broadly appealing shows that appeal to the widest possible audiences, streamers also pursue more mature and intense material that may only attract the interest of niche viewers. While these darker, more disturbing shows may be tough to stomach for more sensitive audiences, they have dramatic potential that has not previously been unlocked. Prestige television has replaced cinema as the best medium for telling mature stories for adult viewers . While the yearly box office is often populated by comic book adaptations, animated titles, and other existing franchises, audiences can expect more well-realized storytelling at home on streaming. Here are the ten darkest television dramas of the last ten years, ranked. 10 \'Perry Mason\' (2020–2023) Chris Chalk as Paul Drake in Perry Mason Season 2 Image via HBO Perry Mason was a radical reboot of a classic television show that took a much darker approach to the story of an idiosyncratic private investigator who became a criminal defense lawyer. Fresh off his Emmy Award-winning performance in The Americans , Matthew Rhys created a new, more complex version of the titular protagonist, who had been struggling with post-traumatic stress disorder following his service in World War I. The series also dealt with the economic depression of the 1930s in a realistic way. Perry Mason did not shy away from disturbing material , as the first two seasons included infanticide, cult indoctrination, political corruption, racial prejudice, and calculated murder. Although the series had the potential to be one of the best crime shows in HBO’s history, Perry Mason was sadly canceled after its second season , despite setting up some intriguing notes on where another season could go. 9 \'Ozark\' (2017–2022) A man and woman look behind them with serious expressions in Ozark. Image via Netflix Ozark became one of the biggest hits in Netflix’s history, and it\'s still not entirely clear why; while the streamer had no problem attracting audiences to a more family-friendly series like Wednesday , Ozark was a dark, shocking, and consistently cruel crime epic about the choices that turn empathetic members of a family into monsters. Ozark was frequently one of the darkest and most shocking shows on television, particularly due to the number of named characters that met their brutal ends. It was particularly shocking to see Jason Bateman , an actor best known for his comedic work, take on a character who was similar to Bryan Cranston ’s Walter White in Breaking Bad . However, it was Laura Linney ’s performance as his sinister wife, Wendy Byrde, that was most unpredictable and immune to intimidation, and truly became the “Lady Macbeth” of the Ozark universe. 8 \'Midnight Mass\' (2021) Hamish Linklater as Father Paul in \'Midnight Mass\' Image via Netflix Midnight Mass is a work of psychological horror that only Mike Flanagan would have been capable of , as he’s been a showrunner who can merge horrific supernatural imagery with deeply personal stories about grief and shame. Midnight Mass may have begun as an emotional character drama about a family’s black sheep returning home after a tragic accident, but it became one of the most disturbing examinations of religious fanaticism in contemporary media. There haven’t been many television villains in recent years who have been as terrifying as Hamish Linklater in Midnight Mass , as he played a demented priest with a sinister agenda brilliantly. Even for those who would broadly consider themselves to be “horror buffs,” the last few episodes of Midnight Mass are so emotionally upsetting and viscerally disturbing that it may be hard to stomach without looking away a few times. 7 \'Killing Eve\' (2018–2022) Jodie Comer as Villanelle in a bubblegum-pink dress sitting on a couch staring into space in Killing Eve. Image via BBC Killing Eve is one of the most psychologically intense spy thrillers of the decade , as it examines a complex relationship that emerged between a MI5 agent ( Sandra Oh ) and a ruthless assassin ( Jodie Comer ). Although the early seasons of Killing Eve did have a very dark sense of humor, the series got progressively darker as it continued, and the body count began to rise. Killing Eve took a realistic approach to the corruption within espionage agencies and showed how often it was for deaths to be covered up without any acknowledgment. Although the series was praised for how it tackled misogyny and harassment in the workplace in a realistic way, the controversial finale of its fourth and final season was so bleak that some of the show’s most vocal fans began to turn on it for committing the “bury your gays” trope. 6 \'The Last of Us\' (2023–) Pedro Pascal with a gun in the woods next to Bella Ramsey in The Last of Us Image via HBO The Last of Us had immense pressure to live up to one of the most acclaimed video games of all time, and HBO certainly spared no expense with one of their most expensive shows ever. Those concerned that The Last of Us would end up sanding off some of the edges of the original material had no reason to be concerned; it wasn’t long into the pilot episode that Joel ( Pedro Pascal ) experiences an unimaginable loss, and becomes a bruised, disturbed anti-hero. The Last of Us wasn’t just a highly disturbing (and eerily prescient) look at an apocalyptic scenario , but an exploration of how desperate circumstances can turn people into the worst versions of themselves. The second episode of the show’s second season featured a moment so graphic, shocking, and upsetting to watch that it drew comparisons to “The Red Wedding” from Game of Thrones . 5 \'Andor\' (2022–2025) Image via Disney+ Andor became the best entry in the Star Wars franchise since The Empire Strikes Back because it showed a side of the universe where there were no Force powers or Jedi Knights. Instead, the amazing prequel series showed how the atrocities committed by the Galactic Empire led a group of brave resistance fighters to start a rebellion movement, even if it meant suffering significant casualties and making unimaginable sacrifices. Andor had an inherent darkness baked into its premise , as those who had already seen Rogue One: A Star Wars Story knew that Cassian Andor ( Diego Luna ) was going to end up sacrificing his life for the Rebel Alliance. However, the show certainly did not shy away from showing the consequences of ignoring fascism, as the second season depicted a brutal act of genocide that sparked disturbing parallels to recent world events. 4 \'The Underground Railroad\' (2021) Image via Prime Video The Underground Railroad is a work of groundbreaking historical fiction that almost feels like an eight-hour film, which may be because the entire series was written and directed by Barry Jenkins , the Academy Award-winning director of the Best Picture winner Moonlight . Set during the Civil War, The Underground Railroad examines the network of systems that allowed slaves to escape to freedom as a literal railroad system operated by a brave group of resistance fighters. The Underground Railroad did not shy away from showing one of the bleakest chapters in American history , as contemporary media has rarely been able to wrestle with the ramifications of racial violence in the Civil War. Although it makes for a frequently upsetting watch, The Underground Railroad will stand the test of time as a truly transcendent work of art that has the power to educate and illuminate. 3 \'True Detective\' (2014–) A woman holds a tool up to a wall in True Detective. Image via HBO True Detective may have begun with its inaugural season in 2014, but it went to even darker and unusual places within its next three seasons. The show has yet to come up with any characters and mysteries that are as compelling as those featured in the first season, but it has still managed to get shockingly dark with each progressive installment, even by the standards of HBO. True Detective is a compelling anthology show because of how different each season is ; the second season examined a conspiracy relevant to the infrastructure of Los Angeles, the second explored a decade-spanning murder case with racial undertones, and the fourth installment, "Night Country," delved into psychological folk horror with its supernatural undertones. There is a significant amount of anticipation for the upcoming fifth season, which will see Nicolas Cage taking on another dramatic role after his recent success with Pig and Longlegs . 2 \'The White Lotus\' (2021–) Image via HBO The White Lotus is a show that has consistently redefined any expectations of genre, because it was initially greenlit as a limited series before being renowned and turning into an engaging multi-season drama. There is certainly a component of satire to each season, but the comedy is very dark, and never hides the fact that the show is about the worst versions of people who seek solace from their miserable lives on vacation. Each season of The White Lotus has gotten progressively bleaker , and the third season even attracted some backlash from viewers who felt that Mike White had crossed a line. It’s because of how powerful the performances are and how memorable the characters become that The White Lotus feels like such an event, and why its unpredictable series of twists and turns end up provoking such extreme viewer responses. 1 \'Mindhunter\' (2017–2019) Jonathan Groff in a suit and tie walking through a prison in Mindhunter. Image via Netflix Mindhunter is one of the best crime shows in recent memory, as David Fincher was able to take everything he had learned about serial killers from his work in film and turn it into an exciting series. Mindhunter examined the career of FBI Agent Holden Ford ( Jonathan Groff ), based on the real John Douglas, who developed an analytical approach to assessing serial killers in order to learn more about their psychology and patterns of behavior. Mindhunter explored some of the most disturbing and infamous true crime cases of all time , including the Atlanta child murders, the Manson family massacre, and the BTK killer. Beyond the show’s frequent use of graphic content, Mindhunter made the disturbing assertion that there were psychopaths living in normal conditions who could be set off to make violent decisions if they were triggered to do so. mindhunter-tv-poster.jpg Like Follow Followed Mindhunter TV-MA Crime Drama Thriller Release Date 2017 - 2019 Showrunner Joe Penhall Cast See All Jonathan Groff Holt McCallany Where to watch Close WHERE TO WATCH Streaming Genres Crime, Drama , Thriller Powered by Expand Collapse Google is updating how content is shown. ABC, CBS, and NBC aired nothing. PBS offered a dismissive brief. How about NPR’s All Things Considered? You won’t believe what they considered. Chairman James Comer summarized: “The Biden Autopen Presidency will go down as one of the biggest political scandals in U.S. history. As Americans saw President Biden’s decline with their own eyes, Biden’s inner circle sought to deceive the public, cover-up his decline, and took unauthorized executive actions with the autopen that are now invalid." There was an NPR segment lasting 4.5 minutes. But it never mentioned any of the Republican findings. They only interviewed an expert to explain the Republicans couldn’t possibly reverse any pardons Biden signed with an autopen! They were only concerned that Biden’s pardons remain valid, and who cares about Biden’s incapacity to be president? Anchor Ailsa Chang barely mentioned Congressman Comer, which is very much an NPR pattern. Not only has NPR failed to interview Comer, a look at the search engine on NPR.org finds more results for English actress Jodie Comer. I found two James Comer results. You can find a story from December 15, 2023 that sounded like DNC opposition research. On Morning Edition, they interviewed AP reporter Brian Slodysko, who claimed Comer had a shell company, just like Hunter Biden. Comer called that story financially illiterate. NPR host Leila Fadel cued up the AP man: “The big takeaway in your story is that the accusations that are being leveled against President Biden\'s son are very similar to what you\'ve reported on Comer. If you could, talk about that.” The only other search result is a James Comer interview in 2017 about the firing of James Comey – that can get confusing. In the latest report, Comer was mentioned in passing as anchor Ailsa Chang interviewed Minnesota law professor Mark Osler, who penned an op-ed last year promoting Gov. Tim Walz to be Kamala Harris’s running mate. Don\'t miss the part where Chang feels she must underline this is a "Republican-led committee," so NPR fans can roll their eyes: NPR\'s All Things Considered October 28, 2025 AILSA CHANG: So this House Oversight Committee accuses the Biden White House of covering up Biden\'s cognitive decline. Let me just ask you, what does this report ultimately ask for? MARK OSLER: Well, it\'s asking for a further investigation by the Department of Justice. I think they were frustrated because some of the witnesses pled the Fifth. And there\'s a political point being made as well. CHANG: OK. And just to remind everyone, this is a Republican-led committee. What do you make of the argument that they lay out in this report about Biden\'s cognitive decline and the permanence of these preemptive pardons? OSLER: Yeah. I\'m not an expert on cognition, but I am an expert on clemency, and I can tell you that the Constitution doesn\'t make any requirement whatsoever as to how a pardon or a commutation is going to be put into writing or issued at all. And we\'ve seen a variety of methods used over the years. You know, in 2005, the Office of Legal Counsel provided the president with advice that the president could use an autopen to sign bills - obviously one of the most important things the president is going to sign. And since then, presidents have used autopens for a wide variety of things... CHANG: Right. OSLER: ...Especially when there\'s a lot to be signed at once. CHANG: Well, what can the Department of Justice actually do in this situation? Like, can you think of anytime a pardon from a president has been reversed or declared null and void, as this House committee and President Trump would like to see happen here? OSLER: No, that hasn\'t happened. Once a president issues a pardon, it\'s been viewed as final. And so if something was to get overturned here, this would really be breaking new ground. CHANG: So are you telling me that a president\'s pardon power is absolute? OSLER: It\'s surprising, but that\'s what it says in the Constitution. It\'s almost absolute. It can\'t cover people who are under impeachment, and it\'s generally accepted that it can\'t pardon future crimes, those that haven\'t been committed yet. But yes. It\'s really rare in having so few checks and balances. CHANG: Well, then, okay. Say you\'re a person who did receive a pardon from President Biden. What would you advise that person to do to protect themselves legally now from having that pardon reversed or somehow invalidated during the Trump administration? OSLER: Yeah. There\'s really not that much that they can do. Again, I think most people who have studied this would be shocked if a pardon was overturned. One of the things that I really fear that could happen with this investigation and some of the conclusions that they seem to want to reach is you have 37 people who received a commutation of their death sentence by President Biden. And I would really think it would cause a constitutional crisis if President Trump moved to execute those people despite that commutation of the death sentence. Published Fri, 21 Nov 2025 09:47:03 -0600 by Aedan Juvet | Comments Article Summary Lady Gaga addresses the backlash and mixed reviews surrounding Joker: Folie À Deux\'s release. Joker: Folie À Deux underperformed at the box office despite high expectations from fans and critics. Gaga reveals she felt "artistically rebellious" when joining the Joker sequel and poured herself into the role. The intense online reactions initially amused Gaga but eventually became painful due to her emotional investment. For years, the sequel to Joker was framed as one of the big comic book events on the calendar. The first film even earned more than $1 billion worldwide and picked up a stack of Oscar nominations, so expectations for the follow-up were pretty huge. Instead, Joker: Folie à Deux landed with far less-than-thrilling numbers, earning about $207 million on a reported budget of $190 to $200 million, with most labeling its run as a box office bomb. Unfortunately, the audience reaction was just as rocky. The musical legal drama currently sits around a 31% approval rating with critics and a 31% with audiences on Rotten Tomatoes, along with a rare \'D\' grade from audiences via CinemaScore. Still, it\'s not all bad, as reviews have ranged from praise for its audacity and craft to frustration with its story, tone, and treatment of Arthur Fleck and Harley Quinn, leaving both critics and general moviegoers sharply divided about its overall execution. Now, Lady Gaga , who joins the sequel as a reimagined Harley named Lee Quinzel, recently spoke to Rolling Stone about what it was like to pour everything into the film and watch that backlash unfold. © 2024 Warner Bros. Lady Gaga Was Feeling Artistically Rebellious When She Signed on to Joker: Folie à Deux In the interview, she acknowledged that there was a ton of negativity around Joker and said she had been feeling "artistically rebellious" when she first signed on to the project. She also revealed that, at first, the intensity of the reactions made her laugh, since it was "just getting so unhinged," but the noise eventually started to sting. She then admitted she was not entirely unfazed by the backlash and said it became more painful as the discourse dragged on, especially because she had put so much of herself into the role (and we all know how reactive the internet can be). In Joker: Folie à Deux, the story picks up with Arthur Fleck locked in Arkham and awaiting trial for his crimes as Joker. Struggling with his sense of self, he finds both a warped kind of love and an outlet through music, with the film built around a mix of jukebox numbers and original material that blur the line between fantasy and reality. The cast once again centers Joaquin Phoenix as Arthur alongside Gaga\'s Lee, with supporting roles from Brendan Gleeson , Catherine Keener , Zazie Beetz , Steve Coogan, and others, all under the direction of Todd Phillips . Joker: Folie à Deux may not have become the cultural juggernaut many expected, but its messy reception, polarizing choices, and Gaga\'s candid response have kept it in the conversation long after its theatrical run, now continuing on streaming. By Bollywood Hungama News Network - October 30, 2025 - 12:41 PM IST Singer-turned-actor Lisa Mishra continues to establish herself as a multi-dimensional artist. Seamlessly balancing her dual careers in music and acting, Mishra has also ventured into live performances and podcasting, carving out a unique creative identity that transcends traditional boundaries. Lisa Mishra credits Lady Gaga as inspiration for her multi-faceted journey of being a singer and an actor: “She motivates me to embrace all sides of myself” Drawing parallels with global icons who redefine artistic expression, Lisa acknowledges Lady Gaga as a major influence on her journey. “I’ve always been deeply inspired by artists like Lady Gaga, who don’t limit their creative and artistic expression to music alone. She seamlessly blends performance, acting, and storytelling into her journey and that motivates me to embrace all sides of myself, whether it’s singing, acting, performing live, or even connecting with audiences through my podcast,” said Mishra. Lisa Mishra, who first gained recognition for her distinctive voice in chart-topping tracks, has steadily expanded her repertoire, venturing into acting and recently making her presence felt in the OTT space. In addition to her music and screen work, she has also launched her own podcast, further engaging with audiences and offering insight into her world as a creator. Her dynamic trajectory reflects the evolution of contemporary Indian artists, who are no longer confined to a single medium. By embracing multiple forms of expression, Lisa Mishra is positioning herself among the new generation of performers who are redefining creativity with authenticity and impact. Gaga talked about her mental health in detail in an interview with Rolling Stone on Thursday, November 13. Lady Gaga has received seven nominations at the Grammy Awards.(Charles Sykes/Invision/AP) The pop sensation, whose real name is Stefani Germanotta, disclosed that she had filmed A Star Is Born on lithium. After the film was completed, Gaga embarked on a belated tour in support of her 2016 album Joanne. One night, Gaga had experienced what she described as a “psychotic break.” Lady Gaga’s revelation “I did A Star Is Born on lithium. There was one day that my sister said to me, ‘I don’t see my sister anymore.’ And I canceled the tour. There was one day I went to the hospital for psychiatric care. I needed to take a break. I couldn’t do anything… I completely crashed,” Gaga told Rolling Stone. Gaga said all this was “really scary.” “There was a time where I didn’t think I could get better.… I feel really lucky to be alive. I know that might sound dramatic, but we know how this can go,” she added. (Photo by Manny Carabel/Getty Images for MTV) The singer is on the cover of Rolling Stone , out Thursday, and she comes clean about using a drug to treat and prevent episodes of mania while filming the Oscar-nominated film. Once filming wrapped, she hit the road for her Joanne world tour, and this is where she experienced what she describes as a psychotic break. The Oscar winner says, “There was one day that my sister said to me, ‘I don’t see my sister anymore,’” Gaga told the outlet. “And I canceled the tour. There was one day I went to the hospital for psychiatric care. I needed to take a break. I couldn’t do anything I completely crashed. It was really scary. There was a time where I didn’t think I could get better. I feel really lucky to be alive. I know that might sound dramatic, but we know how this can go.” VENICE, ITALY - SEPTEMBER 04: Lady Gaga attends the "Joker: Folie A Deux" photocall during the 81st Venice International Film Festival at Palazzo del Casino on September 04, 2024 in Venice, Italy. (Photo by Stephane Cardinale - Corbis/Corbis via Getty Images) It probably didn’t help that this period of time was one of the busiest for Lady Gaga. Not only was she starring alongside Bradley Cooper in “A Star is Born,” which earned her two Oscar nominations, she also headlined the Super Bowl Halftime Show and released her “Joanne" album. She also embarked on a very long and viral press tour for the film, running through the Oscars in February 2019, where the “Shallow” singer won for best original song. Time and healing have passed and Gaga has found love with fiancé Michael Polansky and is now a “healthy, whole person.” FILE - Lady Gaga performs during the 67th annual Grammy Awards on Feb. 2, 2025, in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Chris Pizzello, File) “Being in love with someone that cares about the real me made a very big difference,” Gaga says of her boyfriend, whom she began dating in 2020. Up next for the “Bad Romance” singer was starring in “Joker: Folie a Deux,” the sequel to the Oscar-winning “Joker” opposite Joaquin Phoenix. The 2024 film did not meet critics’ or audiences’ expectations, with a domestic opening of $37.8 million. “I wasn’t, like, unfazed,” Gaga says about “Joker’s” reception. “It’s funny, I’m almost nervous to share my reaction. But the truth is, when it first started happening, I started laughing. Because it was just getting so unhinged. When it takes a while for something to kind of dissipate, that can be a little bit more painful. Only because I put a lot of myself into it.” LONDON, ENGLAND - SEPTEMBER 25: Lady Gaga attends the UK Premiere of "Joker: Folie à Deux" at Cineworld Leicester Square on September 25, 2024 in London, England. (Photo by Dave Benett/WireImage) The 39-year-old added, “There was a ton of negativity around ‘Joker.\' And I think I was feeling artistically rebellious at the time.” Gaga channeled all the negativity in her “Disease” music video, the first single from her newest album, “Mayhem.” FILE - Lady Gaga arrives at the 64th annual Grammy Awards at the MGM Grand Garden Arena on Sunday, April 3, 2022, in Las Vegas. A gunman accused of shooting and seriously wounding the singer\'s dog walker and stealing her two French bulldogs was mistakenly released from jail on Wednesday, April 6 and is being sought, authorities said Friday, April 8. (Photo by Jordan Strauss/Invision/AP, File) “I put so much of that energy into that video. I was in that place, you know, I was like, ‘I’ll show you who I am, and I’ll show you what this fight is like,’” she said. But now, going into the 2026 Grammys, Gaga is the second-most-nominated artist of the night with seven nods. “Mayhem” was nominated for album of the year, while the mega-successful single “Abracadabra” (which debuted during last year’s Grammys) nabbed record and song of the year nods. Kirk in Star Trek , recently declined an opportunity to participate in the reality TV show Dancing with the Stars . At 94, Shatner has a wealth of options at his disposal but stated that the show would require “too much” commitment. William Shatner’s Career and Recent Ventures Shatner continues to be a prolific figure in entertainment. His latest project includes a spoken-word album titled Bill , which was crafted during the COVID-19 pandemic. Collaborators on the album include notable artists such as Brad Paisley, John Lurie, and Joe Jonas. The album, released by Jonas’s Let’s Get It! Records and Republic Records, showcases Shatner’s personal history through poetic narratives. Shatner worked remotely with his team, utilizing phone calls and Zoom for collaboration during the pandemic. Shatner’s Thoughts on Dancing with the Stars In a conversation with AV Club, Shatner expressed admiration for Dancing with the Stars and its host, Tom Bergeron. He recalled how he was invited to participate many times but ultimately turned down the offer due to time constraints, stating, “I was busy. They needed like three months; it was too much.” Oldest Contestant: Cloris Leachman, 82 years old. Youngest Contestant: Willow Shields, 14 years old. Shatner’s age and the physical demands of the show influenced his decision. The actor famously went to space at 90 years old, where he described his experience as filled with “overwhelming sadness,” prompting reflections on humanity’s impact on the planet in his book Boldly Go: Reflections on a Life of Awe and Wonder . Final Thoughts Despite his declining the invitation, Shatner is still very much a creative force, open to diverse opportunities. Beloved for her authenticity and emotional intensity, she\'s the kind of actor who can ground even the most fantastical story in truth. On Letterboxd , a platform where cinephiles value performance, storytelling, and craft, Lawrence\'s best-rated movies reveal not just her range, but the kind of work that resonates most deeply with thoughtful movie lovers everywhere. What\'s striking about Lawrence\'s highest-rated movies is how they capture different stages of her evolution as an artist. Across these roles, she manages to present complex characters who are fighters, survivors, outcasts. Her projects not only showcase her acting chops but also engage with themes like identity, resilience, and morality that resonate strongly with the Letterboxd community. Ultimately, Jennifer Lawrence\'s top-rated movies on Letterboxd tell a story of artistic integrity and evolution . 10 \'The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 2\' (2015) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.4/5 Natalie Dormer next to Jennifer Lawrence drawing a bow and arrow in The Hunger Games: Mockingjay Part 2. Image via Lionsgate The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 2 concludes Katniss Everdeen\'s (Lawrence) journey as she leads the rebellion against the oppressive Capitol . After being manipulated by both sides, Katniss joins a covert mission with Gale ( Liam Hemsworth ), Finnick ( Sam Claflin ), and Peeta ( Josh Hutcherson ) to assassinate President Snow ( Donald Sutherland ) and end the conflict once and for all. As they navigate a deadly, booby-trapped Capitol, they face devastating losses. Since Katniss Everdeen is one of Lawrence\'s most well-known roles, it makes sense that Letterboxd users would rate all The Hunger Games movies as some of her best projects. In particular, it makes sense that fans would highlight The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 2 , since it brings Katniss\' story to a close. Of all The Hunger Games movies, it\'s clear that this one resonates with fans because Lawrence shows how far Katniss has come . 9 \'Causeway\' (2022) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.4/5 Jennifer Larence as Lynsey looking outside her window in Causeway. Image via Apple TV Causeway introduces Lynsey (Lawrence), a U.S. Army engineer who suffers a traumatic brain injury while serving in Afghanistan and returns home to New Orleans to recover. Struggling with memory loss, emotional instability, and a sense of disconnection, she moves in with her mother and tries to rebuild her life. As she grapples with the desire to return to active duty, Lynsey forms an unexpected friendship with James ( Brian Tyree Henry ), a local mechanic coping with his own trauma. Causeway is a compassionate portrayal of PTSD and highlights real issues veterans face every day. The movie represents Lawrence\'s return to the kind of intimate, emotionally grounded storytelling that first earned her critical acclaim and has made her fans appreciate her work . It makes sense that Causeway would resonate with Letterboxd users since it highlights Lawrence\'s ability to portray a deeply relatable character with subtlety and nuance. 8 \'Die My Love\' (2025) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.4/5 Grace (Jennifer Lawrence) and Jackson (Robert Pattinson) dancing together in \'Die My Love\' Image via MUBI Die My Love is a psychological drama that follows Grace (Lawrence) and Jackson ( Robert Pattinson ), a young couple who move from New York City to rural Montana to live in Jackson\'s childhood home, seeking a quieter life after the birth of their child. As Grace struggles with post-partum depression, she slips into isolation and confusion as her mental health worsens . Grace and Jackson\'s relationship also deteriorates as Grace\'s inner world becomes more chaotic. Die My Love gives Lawrence the space to deliver one of her most visceral and vulnerable performances to date, which makes it stand out among Letterboxd users. Die My Love dives deeply into complex themes like the realities of motherhood, mental illness, and feminine rage with unflinching honesty . Lawrence showcases the fact that she can elevate any partnership or ensemble she\'s part of, which makes this one of her most notable works . 7 \'Mother!\' (2017) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.5/5 Him guiding Mother through a crowd of strangers Image via Paramount Pictures Mother! is a psychological horror movie that follows a young woman living with her poet husband in a secluded house she has painstakingly rebuilt after a fire . Their tranquil life unravels when uninvited guests arrive, first a mysterious couple and then a chaotic flood of people who invade their home, which completely upends their lives. As events spiral into violence and destruction, the story morphs into a disturbing metaphor for creation. It makes sense that Mother! is one of Jennifer Lawrence\'s highest-rated projects by Letterboxd users because it’s the kind of bold, divisive, and symbolically rich movie fans have come to expect from her. Lawrence\'s emotionally raw, physically demanding portrayal of a mother anchors the chaos and gives the movie its human core . Mother! is exactly the kind of movie that so many viewers respond to since it\'s so unique and unforgettable. 6 \'Winter\'s Bone\' (2010) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.5/5 Jennifer Lawrence as Ree standing next to her horse in \'Winter\'s Bone\' Image via Roadhouse Attractions Winter\'s Bone follows 17-year-old Ree Dolly (Lawrence) as she struggles to keep her impoverished family together in the Ozark Mountains. When her missing father, out on bail after serving time for a drug charge, puts their home up as bond collateral, Ree must find him before they lose everything . Her search leads her through a harsh, secretive rural community steeped in poverty, crime, and silence. She has only herself to rely on as she tries to do what\'s best for her family. It makes sense that Letterboxd users would highlight Winter\'s Bone as one of Lawrence\'s best movies because it\'s an early example of her talent and range as an artist. Through her character, Lawrence explores the realities that many living in rural America face . The movie\'s quiet intensity, social realism, and moral complexity make it a standout example of early-2010s American indie cinema , a genre in which Lawrence made a name for herself. 5 \'X-Men: First Class\' (2011) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.6/5 Charles Xavier (James McAvoy), Magneto (Michael Fassbender), Mystique (Jennifer Lawrence), Moira MacTaggert (Rose Byrne), Beast (Nicholas Hoult), Havok (Lucas Till), and Banshee (Caleb Landry Jones), standing outside in X-Men: First Class Image via 20th Century Studios X-Men: First Class is a superhero origin story that explores the beginnings of the X-Men and the ideological divide between future rivals Charles Xavier ( James McAvoy ) and Magneto ( Michael Fassbender ). Set during the Cold War and the Cuban Missile Crisis, the film follows young mutants discovering their powers and banding together to stop the powerful mutant Sebastian Shaw ( Kevin Bacon ), who plans to trigger global nuclear war to wipe out humanity. It makes sense that X-Men: First Class is one of Jennifer Lawrence\'s highest-rated projects by Letterboxd users because it stands out as a stylish, character-driven reinvention of the superhero genre. Unlike many formulaic comic-book movies, First Class blends political history, emotional depth, and sleek 1960s aesthetics with well-drawn characters and moral complexity. As Mystique, Lawrence proves that she could always hold her own in big franchises and stand out in a crowd . 4 \'X-Men: Days of Future Past\' (2014) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.7/5 Jennifer Lawrence as Mystique looking intently in the 2014 movie X-Men: Days of Future Past Image via 20th Century Studios X-Men: Days of Future Past is a continuation of First Class , and a time-bending superhero epic that unites the casts of the original X-Men trilogy. In a dystopian future where mutant-hunting Sentinels have nearly exterminated both mutants and humans who aid them , the surviving X-Men send Wolverine\'s ( Hugh Jackman ) consciousness back to 1973 to prevent the war’s origins. His mission is to convince a disillusioned young Charles Xavier and an embittered Magneto to work together and stop Mystique. It makes sense that X-Men: Days of Future Past is one of Jennifer Lawrence\'s highest-rated projects by Letterboxd users because it represents the X-Men franchise at its creative and emotional peak . If First Class proved Lawrence could hold her own in a massive franchise, X-Men: Days of Future Past proved she could be a leader. Lawrence\'s role as Mystique is pivotal . She\'s not just a shapeshifting fighter but the emotional core of the story, whose moral choices determine the fate of mutantkind. 3 \'Silver Linings Playbook\' (2012) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.7/5 Jennifer Lawrence, who is wearing her hair in a ponytail and a black shirt, glares at Bradley Cooper, who is wearing a number 10 Eagles jersey, in Silver Linings Playbook. Image via The Weinstein Company Silver Linings Playbook is a romantic dramedy that follows Pat Solitano ( Bradley Cooper ), a man struggling with bipolar disorder after a violent breakdown, as he tries to rebuild his life after a stint in a mental health facility . Determined to reconcile with his estranged wife, he moves back in with his parents, Dolores ( Jacki Weaver ) and Pat ( Robert De Niro ). He meets Tiffany (Lawrence), a young widow dealing with her own grief and emotional instability. Silver Linings Playbook stands out with Letterboxd users because it perfectly showcases her emotional range, comedic timing, and naturalistic acting style. Lawrence\'s portrayal of Tiffany as a complex, impulsive, and deeply empathetic woman feels raw and authentic, grounding the movie\'s blend of chaos and charm. Silver Linings Playbook balances its indie with a story that earned mainstream appeal, making it one of Lawrence\'s most beloved and respected works . 2 \'The Hunger Games\' (2012) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.8/5 The Hunger Games is a dystopian drama that is the first chapter in the franchise. The story is set in the totalitarian nation of Panem, where the ruling Capitol forces 12 impoverished districts to send a boy and a girl each year to fight to the death in a televised event known as the Hunger Games. When her younger sister Prim ( Willow Shields ) is chosen as a tribute, 16-year-old Katniss Everdeen (Lawrence) volunteers to take her place, joining Peeta Mellark as District 12\'s representatives. It makes sense that The Hunger Games is one of Jennifer Lawrence\'s highest-rated projects by Letterboxd users because it\'s a rare blockbuster that combines thrilling entertainment with strong social commentary. This movie proves beyond a doubt that Lawrence can shine in a blockbuster franchise while elevating the performances of those around her . Lawrence\'s performance anchors the story with authenticity and quiet strength, turning a popular book adaptation into a genuinely respected project . 1 \'The Hunger Games: Catching Fire\' (2013) Average Letterboxd Rating: 3.9/5 Josh Hutcherson as Peeta and Jennifer Lawrence as Katniss look pensive in The Hunger Games: Catching Fire. Image via Lionsgate The Hunger Games: Catching Fire continues Katniss Everdeen\'s story as she becomes a reluctant symbol of hope after surviving the Hunger Games with fellow tribute Peeta Mellark. Katniss struggles with trauma and guilt while trying to protect her loved ones from President Snow , who sees her defiance as a threat to his power. To crush her growing influence, Snow announces the "Quarter Quell," a special edition of the Games that forces previous victors to compete again. The Hunger Games: Catching Fire being Jennifer Lawrence\'s highest-rated movie on Letterboxd makes sense because it\'s widely considered the artistic and emotional peak of the Hunger Games franchise . This chapter of the story features a darker tone and a clear sense of purpose, which makes it stand out . This movie highlights how much Lawrence understands Katniss, since she compassionately showcases the trauma she\'s lived through. Thirty-two teams start the week with the dream of winning it all, but only four will hoist the big trophy. The first round is on Thursday for all four classes. Friday features consolation and semifinal matches. Saturday will have consolation, third-place, and championship games. All the title matches start at 4:30 p.m. WYOPREPS 2025 VOLLEYBALL STATE CHAMPIONSHIP PREVIEW WyoPreps is previewing the volleyball state championships with a look at each classification. We break down the favorites, other top contenders, and stats leaders playing in the state tournament based on access to official team stats through WyoPreps weekly reports or online team pages. Class 1A Defending champion Little Snake River has been the top team most of the 2025 season. The Rattlers enter the state tournament with a 29-3 record and are coming off a 1A West Regional crown. LSR is led by Kenzie Evans, who has a class-best 435 kills, which is an average of 5.6 kills per set. Setter Bailey Myers dishes out an average of 10.2 assists per set, and Melanie Cozzens is averaging 6.4 digs per set. Cokeville was last year’s runner-up, and the Panthers have been among the top three all season. They are 21-13 on the year with several losses to teams from higher classes. Little Snake River and Cokeville might be on a collision course again. Other contenders include Hulett, who comes off a 1A East Regional title. The Red Devils are 23-6 on the season after not even reaching the regional tournament a year ago. Southeast (25-6), Burlington (24-9), Dubois (19-8), and Upton (19-12) have all shown flashes of making a run at the state tournament. Another top stat performer is Jordynn Speckner from Lingle-Fort Laramie. She averages 7.4 digs per set. Class 2A Defending champ Big Horn has been the team to beat all season. Alli Nikont has a squad that has lost only two matches against 2A competition. The rest of those defeats were to 3A and 4A teams. The Rams enter the state championships with a record of 27-9 this season. Are they the favorites? Probably, but Sundance (24-9) and Tongue River (26-8) have been hot on their trail, and both the Bulldogs and Eagles have a victory over Big Horn this year. Those three are the favorites going into the state championships. The contenders list starts with Greybull (21-9), who won the West regional, but the Buffs do not have a win over the top three. Pine Bluffs (22-8) has played good volleyball, but like Greybull, the Hornets have not been able to get past the big three. Big Piney (14-16) from the 2A Southwest is a dark horse, as the Punchers have been able to play better volleyball at the right time of year. Jaylin Mills from Sundance leads 2A at 4.7 kills per set. Chaney Reish of Tongue River is at 3.8 kills per set. The top setter in 2A this season is Wyatt Whaley of Greybull. She is averaging 9 assists per set. Kaity Shreve from Big Piney is at 8.6 assists per set. Defensively, Sundance’s Blakely Gill tops the leaderboard at 6.2 digs per set, while Lily Maslowski from Tongue River is at 4.9 digs per set. Cody is 33-2 on the season, and their only losses were to 4A No. 1 Kelly Walsh. Yes, they went undefeated versus 3A competition. The Fillies are led by setter Maddie Beaudrie, who averages 9.7 assists per set this season. She has several options to go to on offense this year, including Grace Hays, Ellie Talich, Allison Gee, and Sydney Simone. The Fillies went unbeaten in conference matches and just won the 3A West Regional title last weekend. Chasing Cody is last year’s defending champ, Douglas (29-7). The Bearcats have been No. 2 all season and won the 3A East Regional last week. Then, there’s Lovell (24-6-2), Mountain View (24-13-1), and Torrington (17-13-2), who all turned in very good seasons to finish near the top of the conference standings and played well at regionals. A couple of the top hitters are Leah Ewing of Douglas at 3.9 kills per set, which leads the class, and Addyson Stephens from Mountain View, who is at 3.8 kills per set. Avynn Yost of Douglas is at 9.5 assists per set, right behind Beaudrie of Cody. Newcastle’s Adalyn Olson tops the defensive charts at 5.2 digs per set. Teammate Sydney Peterson is right behind at 5 digs per set. Class 4A The top two programs over the last eight years in the big-school class have been Kelly Walsh and Laramie. Those two schools have won the 4A title during that stretch. The defending champion Trojans are the favorites going into state this year. They are 31-3 on the season and have two head-to-head wins over Laramie, who is 28-3. Those two appear to be on a collision course, but stranger things have happened. Green River (24-5) and Thunder Basin (22-6) are the top contenders, as both have a victory over KW this season. Next are a red-hot Star Valley (19-15) and Evanston (23-16), who have shown the ability to play good volleyball and could be a factor this weekend. Laramie’s Tessa Dodd leads 4A at 5 kills per set. Kyan Lawlar of Evanston has the most kills at 451 or 4.2 kills per set. Those two will square off in round one on Thursday. Green River’s McKinley Killpack is the top setter at 9.3 assists per set, with Piper Martin of Thunder Basin at 8.3 assists per set. Brookelyn Phillips of Green River averages 5.3 digs per set to top the class. Reece McGrath from Thunder Basin is second at 4.5 digs per set. Overview Our bottom line is that until someone beats the champs, WyoPreps thinks Kelly Walsh, Cody, Big Horn, and Little Snake River are the teams to beat in each class. We’ll see how they handle the pressure and who rises to the occasion. Rose disclosed that she was once attached to the project, naming Sweeney a “cr***n” and blaming her of ruining the movie. She stated that the original version was “life changing” and had proper LGBTQ+ representation. Following the backlash over her use of words, Rose cited that she should have said “psychopath.” Global Desk Ruby Rose has publicly criticized Sydney Sweeney, labeling her a “cr***n” and holding her accountable for the disappointing box office performance of Christy . The recently debuted boxing biopic , which stars Sweeney as real-life fighter Christy Martin, has failed to generate an influence commercially despite extensive pre-release promotion. The movie , directed by David Michôd , allegedly achieved just $1.3 million in its opening weekend in the U.S., marking one of the poorest beginnings for a wide-release biopic this year. Ruby Rose’s Posts on Threads In an unexpected social-media outburst, Rose took to Threads to address the movie's weak performance and conveyed her frustrations. She stated that she had once been attached to the project herself, citing, “The original Christy Martin script was incredible. Life changing. I was attached to play Cherry.” As per Rose, the prior team behind Christy had a personal bond to the story’s LGBTQ+ concepts. She said, “Everyone had experience with the core material. Most of us were actually gay. It’s part of why I stayed in acting. Losing roles happens all the time.” Her criticism deepened when she mentioned Sweeney's PR team’s response to the movie’s box office struggles. Rose cited, “For her PR to talk about it flopping and saying SS [Sydney Sweeney] did it for the ‘people’. None of ‘the people’ want to see someone who hates them, parading around pretending to be us. You’re a cr **n, and you ruined the film. Period. Christy deserved better.”* Live Events After followers mentioning out that “cr***n” is regarded as an ableist slur, Rose later cited that her wording, stating, “I regret writing that and should have just said psychopath.” Sweeney’s Response Rose’s comments seemed to be a direct reaction to Sweeney’s Instagram post from Monday, where the Euphoria actress stated that the movie’s underwhelming launch. The dispute erupted after Christy recorded one of the weakest wide openings of the year, prompting heated online reaction from figures in and around the queer community. Rose, who says she was previously attached to the project, published a Threads post excoriating Sweeney and the film\'s public relations narrative. The row has sharpened wider debates about representation, star politics, and how biopics of queer figures are made and marketed. Ruby Rose\'s Post: What She Said and Where She Said It Ruby Rose took to Threads to say the original script for Christy was \'incredible\' and that she had been \'attached to play Cherry\', asserting the project began as a queer-led passion piece. In the post, Rose wrote that \'most of us were actually gay\' and accused Sweeney\'s publicity of reframing the film as something done \'for the people\' while insisting \'none of "the people" want to see someone who hates them, parading around pretending to be us\'. She concluded with the line, \'You\'re a cretin and you ruined the film. Period. Christy deserved better\'. Ruby Rose\'s full Threads post. Threads: rubyrose Rose\'s message quickly circulated across social platforms, prompting responses from critics, fans, and other industry figures. Several news outlets republished the Threads screenshots and reported the post in detail. Box Office, Reception, and the Wider Context Christy opened on 7 November 2025 and posted an opening weekend gross of approximately £900 million ($1,310,888) in the United States across more than 2,000 theatres, a performance that places it among the weakest wide openings of the modern era. Critically, the film has not been uniformly dismissed; critics\' reviews registered mixed-to-positive notices, while audience reactions on some platforms have been enthusiastic, with a very strong Popcornmeter/audience rating reported on Rotten Tomatoes despite the low box office. That gap between commercial performance and audience approval has fuelled the controversy rather than calming it. Industry commentators point to several intersecting factors for the commercial flop. Marketing choices, release timing, and the challenge of turning a complex and painful life story into a mainstream box-office draw. The debate over whether a film\'s cultural impact can be measured by ticket sales has become central to the online conversation. Sweeney\'s Response and Claims About Representation Sydney Sweeney responded publicly on Instagram , defending the film and its purpose, writing she was \'so deeply proud of this movie\' and stressing the project\'s mission to give survivors courage and a platform. A post shared by instagram Sweeney\'s defenders point out that she is the film\'s lead and that many collaborators have spoken in public about the care taken in adapting Christy Martin\'s life. Supporters say an actor\'s personal politics should not necessarily disqualify them from portraying a historical figure, while critics argue that casting choices and off-screen affiliations matter deeply when the subject is part of a marginalised community. Rose\'s allegation that Sweeney \'hates gay people\' draws on a broader context. Sweeney\'s earlier controversies around a fashion campaign and questions about her political registration have left some observers sensitive to whether she is the right figure to represent a queer sports pioneer. Others say accusations of personal bigotry require careful evidence and cannot rest solely on political registration or ad hoc backlash. What This Means For Representation and Biopics The fallout highlights an enduring tension in cinema, who has the right to tell certain stories and how representation is authenticated. For queer audiences and the creative community, the debate over Christy underscores the importance of whose voices are present in writers\' rooms, on set, and in publicity. There is also a pragmatic business lesson. Films that aim to serve activist or corrective cultural purposes still face the marketplace. When a film that foregrounds queer history underperforms, activists and artists inevitably scrutinise whether creative decisions weakened its reach or its resonance. The result is an often painful public reckoning in which artistic intent, casting, marketing, and the lived realities of marginalised communities collide. Ruby Rose\'s intervention has turned what might have been an industry post-mortem into a wider cultural argument about authenticity, allyship, and who benefits when stories about marginalised people make it to the screen. Whether the controversy will lead to changes in casting practices or publicity strategies remains to be seen. The Christy controversy is less about a single film than about who gets to represent a community on a global stage, and the anger born of those perceived betrayals. Christy deserved better,” she added, bashing Sydney Sweeney . It’s been said a million times at this point, but Sydney Sweeney’s cinematic fall from Hollywood It Girl to MAGA-pandering , Bezos-elbow-rubbing , Scooter-Braun-kissing Florida Republican has been nothing short of Shakespearean. This week, Sweeney’s public image suffered at least three more blows: her latest film, Christy , was reported to have one of the worst box office debuts of all time; there are rumors of a possible beef between Sweeney and her Euphoria co-star Zendaya, reportedly due to Sweeney’s seemingly shitty politics; and Ruby Rose just KO’d Sweeney on Threads, adding more insult to more injury. This does nothing to quell my belief that nothing good ever comes from being a Florida Republican. I’m sure Sweeney is fine and is possibly still lip-locked with Braun in Central Park, but I, personally, would never want to show my face outside of Florida ever again after reading Rose’s post. “The original Christy Martin script was incredible. Life changing,” Rose wrote on Threads . “I was attached to play Cherry. Everyone had experience with the core material. Most of us were actually gay. It’s part of why I stayed in acting.” Sweeney’s film is based on the rise of the champion boxer, who was also a victim of domestic violence, and was shot and stabbed by her coach-turned-husband-turned-ex-husband in 2010. “For her PR to talk about it flopping and saying SS did it for the ‘people’. None of ‘the people’ want to see someone who hates them, parading around pretending to be us,” Rose continued. “You’re a cretin and you ruined the film. Period. Christy deserved better.” Brutal. I feel like Rose called me a cretin. Martin has spoken about knowing she was a lesbian since the “5th or 6th grade,” and has long been an advocate for the LGBTQ+ community. But her parents never accepted her sexuality, and she was always nervous about backlash, which, in part, led to her marriage with her abusive ex, who constantly threatened to out her. As a brand new Florida Republican, Sweeney has not spoken out against or denounced the party or state that passed one of the country’s most notorious “Don’t Say Gay” bills—which feels like very cretin-esque behavior to me. For her part, Martin has celebrated the film: “She wasn’t the beautiful, sexy Sydney. She was the tough, rugged Christy in this movie,” she told the audience at the film’s TIFF premiere in September. “And I think it’s awesome. She kicks ass!” OK, let’s not get crazy now… On Monday, Sweeney attempted to shrug off the embarrassing box office numbers, writing on Instagram that “we don’t always just make art for numbers, we make it for impact.” Sure, but if nobody went to see your film because of your flailing public image, then you’re not really doing it for impact either. Yet, imagine the ~impact~ she might have had if, instead of using this press tour—in which she’s promoting a film where she plays a gay female athlete— to blankly stare into the abyss when asked to denounce white supremacy, she used it to denounce the Trump administration’s ceaseless attack on the LGBTQ+ community. Oh, damn! We’ve heard about a secret feud between Sydney Sweeney and Zendaya , allegedly raging behind the scenes on Euphoria . This one? This is going to be loud and proud! Ruby Rose took to her feed on Threads Monday night to put the Anyone But You star on blast… over her new movie! As you may have heard (but not seen because let’s face it, at a $649 per screen average, no one went and saw it), Sydney starred in a movie that dropped over the weekend called Christy . It’s the true story of Christy Martin , the most famous female boxer of her time — whose real battles were behind closed doors as her abusive husband nearly killed her. Christy went on to find her happiness later on — eventually coming out as gay. Go girl! Sydney Sweeney with the real Christy Martin at Variety Power Of Women. / (c) MEGA/WENN So… was this really the right role for Sydney Sweeney, the (accidental?) poster girl of the anti-woke young conservative movement? The openly gay Ruby doesn’t think so! She revealed to her followers that she was attached to a previous iteration of the film — and she hates that Sydney “ruined” it! She wrote: “The original Christy Martin script was incredible. Life changing. I was attached to play Cherry. Everyone had experience with the core material. Most of us were actually gay. It’s part of why I stayed in acting.” Damn! We’re sad for Ruby she didn’t get to make that version. That’s not the issue, as she says “losing roles happens all the time.” What she’s upset about is how Sydney’s people are trying to spin the movie flopping as unimportant — because it was such a labor of love: “For her PR to talk about it flopping and saying SS did it for the ‘people’. None of ‘the people’ want to see someone who hates them, parading around pretending to be us. You’re a cretin and you ruined the film. Period. When asked point-blank about the jeans ad being read as some kind of hidden Nazi propaganda, she basically said she had no comment ! Not to say she never saw it like that, not even just to say she’s vehemently anti-Nazi. Maybe she’s actually fine being thought of as racist… or maybe she doesn’t think she has to prove herself? We really can’t fathom not trying to defend against crazy allegations like that. Meanwhile, you have Sydney the movie star… who’s produced three films that have come out so far. One was a rom com centered around an interracial lesbian wedding, one was a pro-choice allegory horror film, and now this one… All of them are, frankly, pretty damn woke. So is the real Sydney the one making these movies? Or the one Republicans love? Because these conservatives she’s apparently continuing to court ain’t helping her box office any! We mean, certainly the Young Republicans and groypers singing Sweeney’s praises after the American Eagle thing aren’t going to actually go see a lesbian boxer biopic. On the other side of things… Did enough people in the real world skip Christy because, like Ruby Rose, they assume she’s some anti-LGBT crusader in disguise? If so, did she ruin the movie?? The movie follows Millie (Sweeney), a young woman recently released from prison who manages to secure a job as a housekeeper for a wealthy family. Millie works to gain the family\'s trust and becomes closer to the married couple (Seyfried and Sklenar), but soon begins to suspect that some dark secrets may be hiding beneath the facade of happiness and decadence. Via American Eagle PERRY CHIARAMONTE Nov. 11, 2025 09:03 AM ET Gift this article Share Actor Ruby Rose has come out swinging against current it-girl Sydney Sweeney for her current role in a biopic about boxer Christy Martin, claiming that her political beliefs as a registered Republican led to a dismal turnout at theaters. The “Orange Is the New Black” star, 39, took to Threads Monday night to blast the 28-year-old Euphoria actress over her starring role in “Christy” which chronicles the prizefighter and domestic abuse survivor’s life. The film’s dismal weekend debut — one of the worst domestic openings ever for a wide release — sparked fierce debate, culminating in Ms. Rose’s incendiary political attack on the actress. Ms. Rose claimed she was originally cast as Christy — whom she calls “Cherry” — and alleged the initial production team was nearly entirely queer before accusing Sydney of hating gay people. Ruby Rose attends the opening night of “2:22 — A Ghost Story” on July 28, 2023 at Melbourne, Australia. Sam Tabone/Getty Images “The original Christy Martin script was incredible. Life changing. I was attached to play Cherry. Everyone had experience with the core material. Most of us were actually gay. It’s part of why I stayed in acting. Losing roles happens all the time,” she said in a post on Threads . “For her PR to talk about it flopping and saying SS did it for the ‘people’. None of ‘the people’ want to see someone who hates them, parading around pretending to be us. You’re a cretin and you ruined the film. Period. Christy deserved better.” Ms. Rose’s claims that Ms. Sweeney is anti-gay appears to be conjecture as the actress has never publicly made negative statements towards the gay community. Ms. Rose’s diatribe against Ms. Sweeney is just the latest in mounting criticism from left-leaning celebrities since her Republican voter registration became public — scrutiny that intensified amid recent commercial backlash. She has acknowledged that her political affiliation now dominates public perception of her, particularly after her Saturday Night Live hosting gig ignited a firestorm of debate. The controversies peaked earlier this year after she appeared in an American Eagle jeans campaign that drew accusations of racism over a wordplay connecting “jeans” and “genes.” The biopic chronicles Ms. Martin’s meteoric rise as America’s most famous female boxer in the 1990s, her coach-turned-husband’s brutal 2010 attempt on her life, and her struggle with her sexuality. After surviving the attack — her husband received 25 years for attempted second-degree murder—Ms. Martin married former rival Lisa Holewyne in 2017 and became a prominent advocate for domestic violence survivors. The boxer — who earned 49 victories in the ring — has firmly backed Ms. Sweeney, appearing alongside her throughout the film’s promotional tour and undercutting Ms. Rose’s claim. Ms. Sweeney has not directly responded to Ms. Rose’s comments but said on social media that she was proud of the film despite how it fared at the box office. “Proud to represent someone as strong and resilient as Christy Martin. this experience has been one of the greatest honors of my life,” she said in a post on Instagram . “This film stands for survival, courage, and hope. through our campaigns, we’ve helped raise awareness for so many affected by domestic violence. We all signed on to this film with the belief that christy’s story could save lives.” PERRY CHIARAMONTE Mr. Chiaramonte was an investigative reporter and producer at Fox News, a correspondent for the New York Post, and a news editor for the Messenger. Apple TV Morgan Cormack Published: Saturday, 15 November 2025 at 9:00 am Subscribe to Radio Times: 10 weeks for £10, including the Christmas edition Share on facebook Share on twitter Share on pinterest Share on reddit Email to a friend As we continue veering to the anticipated finale of The Morning Show season 4 , we can rest easy in the fact that the candid TV drama is in fact returning for more. Ad It was announced back in September ahead of season 4\'s release that Apple had renewed the series for a fifth instalment. The early renewal didn\'t come as too much of a surprise to fans, seeing as Apple TV had done precisely the same thing ahead of season 3\'s release too. “The Morning Show has been a standout from the very start, debuting as one of the flagship series on Apple TV+. It’s been incredibly rewarding to see it not only entertain but also resonate with audiences worldwide,” said Matt Cherniss, head of programming at Apple TV+. He continued: “Thanks to the outstanding cast and creative team — led by Jennifer, Reese, Charlotte and Mimi — The Morning Show continues to deliver addictively entertaining and provocative stories that we’ve all come to love. We’re excited for viewers to experience the next chapter of this Emmy-winning drama.” But just when will season 5 of The Morning Show be released and who will star? Read on for everything we know so far. The Morning Show season 5 release date speculation Apple TV has not yet announced a release date for the fifth season of The Morning Show so we\'ll just have to wait and see when new episodes are set to come out. However, the show has usually followed a pattern that means seasons are released every couple of years. So, that could very well mean that season 5 will be released in 2027 . The Morning Show season 5 cast: Who will return? Reese Witherspoon as Bradley Jackson and Jennifer Aniston as Alex Levy walk the streets of Manhattan in The Morning Show season 4 poster. Apple TV+ Despite being given an official series renewal, there has been no news of who will be returning to star in the fifth season of The Morning Show. We can imagine that leading stars Reese Witherspoon and Jennifer Aniston will return to helm the series, along with most of the familiar faces of the previous season. Season 4 saw the introduction of William Jackson Harper as the network’s Head of Sports Ben, Marion Cotillard as Celine Dumont, Jeremy Irons as Alex’s father, Aaron Pierre as Miles and Boyd Holbrook as podcaster Brodie. It also saw the return of Billy Crudup, Mark Duplass, Karen Pittman, Nestor Carbonell, Greta Lee, Nicole Beharie and fan-favourite Jon Hamm. The cast members we\'d expect to see in season 5 are as follows. Jennifer Aniston as Alexandra "Alex" Levy Reese Witherspoon as Bradley Jackson Billy Crudup as Cory Ellison Mark Duplass as Charlie "Chip" Black Karen Pittman as Mia Jordan Greta Lee as Stella Bak Nicole Beharie as Christine "Chris" Hunter Jon Hamm as Paul Marks Marion Cotillard as Celine Dumont What will The Morning Show season 5 be about? Reese Witherspoon as Bradley Jackson presenting The Morning Show. Apple TV+ An official synopsis for the fifth season of The Morning Show hasn\'t yet been revealed, but we\'d imagine that it would include some sort of time jump as was the case with the previous season. With the UBA-NBN merger at the forefront of the drama in season 4, we\'d imagine that if the new season did account for a time jump, any tensions surrounding the merger would be ironed out. However, it wouldn\'t be a season of The Morning Show without a fair share of drama, so we can likely look forward to the show continuing to use many real-life scenarios and topical issues for its storylines. Last season explored deepfakes, conspiracy theories and corporate cover-ups in the changing media landscape so there\'s likely plenty more to be explored as the real-life industry continues to change and evolve. Is there a trailer for The Morning Show season 5? No – as production for the fifth season of The Morning Show has yet to kick off, there isn\'t a trailer for it just yet. However, you can watch the trailer for season 4 below. The Morning Show season 4 concludes with its final episode on 19th November and is available to stream on Apple TV+ .
